title: Interpretable multi-omics machine learning reveals unexpected drug mechanisms in Huntington disease models
summary: An interpretable machine-learning model integrated transcriptomic, epigenomic, metabolomic and proteomic data from Huntington-disease cell models to identify previously unknown mechanisms for protective compounds. The analysis predicted autophagy activation for one compound group and mitochondrial-respiration inhibition for another; follow-up imaging, biochemical and energetics assays experimentally confirmed these effects in the cell model.
ai_technology: Interpretable network-optimization model integrating multi-omics over a molecular-interaction network
organization: University of California San Diego and collaborators

evidence.tested: The analysis predicted autophagy activation for one compound group and mitochondrial-respiration inhibition for another; follow-up imaging, biochemical and energetics assays experimentally confirmed these effects in the cell model.
evidence.unknown: Findings were experimentally established in STHdhQ111 murine striatal cells, with autophagy effects also checked in human SH-SY5Y and HEK293 cell lines. The paper notes that the model prioritizes pathways but does not resolve every causal step or demonstrate therapeutic efficacy in patients.
evidence.ai_role: The model integrated multiple omics and prioritized cellular pathways as candidate mechanisms of action; researchers tested those predictions with cellular imaging, biochemical assays and energetics measurements. It revealed unexpected mechanisms for compounds with unrelated known targets.
